zh: 而且我认为对用户来说，他们能感觉到，这并不是关于工作应该如何运作的单一一致愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead it's three different visions that all kind of share a screen and you can hop between, but it is kind of a shipping your org chart style thing that I think users are reacting negatively to.
zh: 相反，它是三个不同的愿景共享同一个屏幕，你可以在它们之间切换，但这有点像把你的组织架构图发布出去，我认为用户对此反应是负面的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we decided let's just start completely from scratch.
zh: 所以我们决定，让我们完全从零开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see where we can get from there.
zh: 让我们看看从那里能走到哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: There might be some really amazing opportunities to bring people from other surfaces into this more bot native experience, but it's really important for people to just have an amazingly simple and amazingly powerful experience.
zh: 也许会有一些非常棒的机会，把人们从其他界面带进这个更原生智能体的体验，但让人们拥有一个极其简单又极其强大的体验是非常重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is a really valuable lesson for people to take away here, just that that might be the solution instead of adding in complicated and existing AI product.
zh: 这是一个非常值得大家在这里吸取的宝贵教训，那就是那可能是解决方案，而不是往复杂的产品里塞进 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So interestingly, Codex went the other direction and it's like a different path than a different product, but it's interestingly, they're like, now we're going to make it one thing.
zh: 所以有意思的是，Codex 走了另一个方向，它是一条不同的路径、一个不同的产品，但有意思的是，他们说，现在我们要把它变成一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's many ways to make it work and it also feels like the path you take there will kind of lead you, but maybe we'll look back and be like, that was not maybe the best idea.
zh: 所以有很多方法可以让它运作，而且你在那里走的路径似乎会引导你，但也许我们回头看会说，那也许不是最好的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something you mentioned that you did that is also really unique is this onboarding of early users.
zh: 你提到你们做的一件事也非常独特，就是早期用户的引导（onboarding）。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard you and your team onboarded two to 300 people manually, including me.
zh: 我听说你和你的团队手动引导了两三百人，包括我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about why you thought that was necessary and what you learned from that experience and just how long that period was of this kind of manual onboarding.
zh: 谈谈你为什么觉得那是必要的，你从那段经历中学到了什么，以及这种手动引导的时期持续了多久。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you just learned so much and the first few onboardings were pretty painful.
zh: 我是说，你就是能学到非常多，最初几次引导相当痛苦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm glad you got a good one, Lenny, but there were some that were kind of rough and we learned a lot.
zh: 我很高兴你得到了一次好的体验，Lenny，但有一些相当艰难，我们学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it was important for the core team to be in the room for those and to just sit on a call for 20 minutes when the computer isn't spinning up or when someone's in onboarding and they're just incredibly confused so that immediately after you're like, that can never happen again.
zh: 我认为核心团队必须在场参与那些引导，在电脑没能启动的时候、或者有人在引导中极其困惑的时候，在电话上坐 20 分钟，这样你立刻就会说，这种事绝不能再发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to solve this tomorrow because tomorrow I'm onboarding this person and it needs to go better.
zh: 我们明天必须解决这个问题，因为明天我要引导下一个人，它必须进行得更顺利。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there was about a two-week period where we were in that mode and onboarded a couple hundred people.
zh: 所以大约有两周的时间我们处于那种状态，引导了几百人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not only did we learn a lot about the product, I think we didn't really know ...
zh: 而且不仅我们对产品学到了很多，我认为我们其实并不真正知道……

speaker: Unknown
en: I think sometimes with these products there's some group think of ways to use them.
zh: 我认为有时对这些产品来说，会存在一些关于使用方式的群体思维。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think internally, because people inside of SpaceXAI were just constantly sharing tips and tricks for how to use Grok Bot, some patterns were starting to emerge that we thought would be useful to the world, but we weren't really sure and we definitely didn't want to bias the world.
zh: 而我认为在内部，因为 SpaceXAI 里的人不断分享如何使用 Grok Bot 的技巧和窍门，一些模式开始浮现，我们认为这些模式对世界会有用，但我们并不真正确定，而且我们绝对不想误导世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there an example of that?
zh: 有这方面的例子吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we rolled out Grok Bot internally, there was about a week or two where the common pattern of the way people would interact with the product was you would have five to 10 bots and each bot you would give a different scope, a different domain, and it was kind of shorthand for different lanes of work.
zh: 当我们向内部推出 Grok Bot 时，大约有一两周的时间，人们与产品交互的常见模式是你会拥有五到十个 bot，你给每个 bot 不同的范围、不同的领域，这有点像不同工作线的简写。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then at around the end of week two, we started to see these messages internally in Slack of people promoting one of their bots who is a bit of a standout performer, and it was like their kind of primary personal assistant promoting that to their chief of staff.
zh: 然后在大约第二周末，我们开始在内部的 Slack 里看到这样的消息，人们提拔他们其中一个表现突出的 bot，它有点像他们的主要私人助理，把它提拔为他们的幕僚长（chief of staff）。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they would actually mostly talk to their chief of staff and the chief of staff would fan out all of these tasks to the other bots and would kind of manage the team.
zh: 然后他们实际上大部分时间都和幕僚长对话，幕僚长会把所有这些任务分发给其他 bot，并有点像管理这个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are some funny screenshots of people actually telling the bot they're promoting that they're promoted and the bot is asking if they get a raise and is their token budget higher, all of these things.
zh: 还有一些有趣的截图，人们真的告诉被提拔的 bot 它被提拔了，bot 问自己能不能加薪、它的 token 预算是不是更高了，诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we kind of took note of that and I think more of the companies started to slightly shift in that direction, but it was not the majority of the company.
zh: 我们注意到了这一点，我认为公司里更多人的用法开始略微朝那个方向转变，但这还不是公司的大多数。

speaker: Unknown
en: People use this product in very different ways.
zh: 人们以非常不同的方式使用这个产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in some of the onboarding sessions and just from the early access program in general, we really did not want to lead the witness and say, create a chief of staff bot, here's exactly the way that that chief of staff should manage all of the other bots and see if early access users would get there themselves.
zh: 所以在一些引导会话中，以及总体上在早期访问计划中，我们真的不想诱导证人，不会说，创建一个幕僚长 bot，幕僚长应该完全按这样管理所有其他 bot，而是看早期访问用户是否会靠自己走到那一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we actually did see that many of them did.
zh: 而我们确实看到他们中很多人做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then we had a bit more of an opinionated take in the product of this feels like a pattern that's working, this feels like a pattern that we should slightly encourage, but it shouldn't be a one-way door.
zh: 于是我们在产品中有了一个更有主见的立场：这感觉是一个行之有效的模式，这是一个我们应该略微鼓励的模式，但它不应该是一个单向门。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there were a few other examples of internal thesis that we really wanted to make sure would bear out in actual external usage without us imposing that in the product.
zh: 还有其他几个内部论点的例子，我们真的很想确保它们在实际的外部使用中得到验证，而不是由我们在产品中强加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there anything else there?
zh: 那里还有其他什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Any examples come to mind?
zh: 能想到什么例子吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think another thing we really tried to pay attention to in the early onboardings was just how much users wanted to see.
zh: 有的,我觉得我们在早期上手引导中真正努力注意的另一件事,就是用户到底想看到多少东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it is something a bit shocking or just different about Grok Bot when you first start using it versus some of the other products that you mentioned, where a lot of the internal mechanics of how Grok Bot works are not shown to the user.
zh: 而且我觉得,当你第一次使用 Grok Bot 时,它会让你有点震惊,或者说与你提到的其他产品不同,那就是 Grok Bot 运行中的很多内部机制是不会展示给用户的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that is we think as these models get smarter, the same way that your teammate, you wouldn't ask for second by second updates of exactly all the buttons they're pressing and websites they're going to.
zh: 原因在于,我们认为随着这些模型变得更聪明,就像你的队友一样,你不会要求他们逐秒汇报他们按下的每一个按钮、访问的每一个网站。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's too much to ask your bots to do that too.
zh: 我认为要求你的智能体也这么做实在是太多了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's honestly just overwhelming and can create more harm than good.
zh: 而且说实话,我觉得那会让人不堪重负,弊大于利。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we moved completely in the other direction of you send a message, you tell your bot to do something, it just starts doing it.
zh: 所以我们完全走向了另一个方向:你发一条消息,你让你的智能体去做某件事,它就直接开始做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sends you progressive updates as it sees fit, and you just see that typing indicator in the little green active circle kind of Slack-like that it's active, it's doing work, it'll get back to you soon.
zh: 它会在它认为合适的时候给你发送阶段性更新,你只会看到那个输入中指示器和小小的绿色活跃圆点,有点像 Slack 那样,表示它处于活跃状态,正在工作,很快会回复你。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you don't see the internal mechanics, you don't see the tool calls, you don't see exactly every little click it's making on its own computer.
zh: 但你看不到内部机制,看不到工具调用,也看不到它在自己电脑上做出的每一个小点击。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we really wanted to take a strong stance that users did not need to see all of those mechanics, and so that's where we started.
zh: 我们真的想表明一个强硬立场:用户不需要看到所有那些机制,这就是我们的起点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did get some feedback that's like, I would love to see my bot's to-do list.
zh: 我们确实收到过一些反馈,比如说,我很想看到我的智能体的待办事项清单。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love to see roughly how it's prioritizing tasks and what it's doing.
zh: 我很想大致看到它是如何排列任务优先级的,以及它在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's great feedback, but it was useful to hear that nobody wanted the long stream of just text streaming out and chain of though sequences.
zh: 这是很好的反馈,但同样有用的是听到没有人想要那种长长的纯文本流式输出和思维链序列。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that also gave us more confirmation that that was the right direction.
zh: 所以这也给了我们更多确认,证明那是正确的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: The fact that you did two to 300 onboarding calls with a small team, I know the team grew over time, but just that is a huge time commitment and you could argue a distraction from the building, clearly not a distraction, clearly a core part of the success.
zh: 你用一个小团队做了两到三百次上手引导通话,我知道团队后来有所扩大,但仅这一点就是巨大的时间投入,你可以说这是对构建工作的分心——显然不是分心,显然是成功的一个核心部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you feel like that's the volume people need to do to figure out what actually needs to happen?
zh: 你觉得这是不是人们需要做的量,才能弄清楚到底需要做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, one thing to emphasize is the early access group is not necessarily just people that are highly influential taste makers.You're in this category, Lenny, and we certainly wanted to get a lot of your feedback just from being very close to many other products on the market and just being a power user of these things.
zh: 嗯,有一点需要强调的是,早期访问群体并不一定只是那些非常有影响力的品味引领者。你就在这个类别里,Lenny,我们当然想从你那里得到很多反馈,因为你对市面上的很多其他产品都非常熟悉,而且这些东西的重度用户。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we also wanted to get early access to more unconventional profiles that we as a company had never really interacted with.
zh: 但我们也想让一些我们公司从未真正接触过的、更非主流的人群获得早期访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one example is there's a coffee shop owner that was a friend of a friend through the company who had heard about Grok Bot, and one day somebody on the core team had shown them a demo of the test flight and got very excited.
zh: 举个例子,有一位咖啡店老板,他是公司里一个朋友的朋友,听说了 Grok Bot,有一天核心团队的某个人给他们演示了 test flight,他们变得非常兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this coffee shop owner ended up being not only amazingly an amazing power user of Grok Bot, but also a rich source of feedback for us.
zh: 结果这位咖啡店老板不仅成了 Grok Bot 惊人的重度用户,还成了我们丰富的反馈来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a very lively thread with many, many bugs that get identified or feature requests, and it's a completely different use case of running a small business.
zh: 我们有一个非常活跃的对话串,里面识别出了很多很多 bug 或功能请求,而这是一种完全不同的用例——经营一家小企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for example, if the Shopify integration was a bit flaky or if it wasn't writing copy for products in a particular way, we would get really rich feedback on that, which is pretty different from the type of feedback we'd get from dog feeding this internally.
zh: 所以举例来说,如果 Shopify 集成有点不稳定,或者它没有以某种特定方式为产品撰写文案,我们就会得到非常丰富的相关反馈,这与我们内部 dogfooding 时得到的反馈类型相当不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think it was an important exercise for us to check our blind spots and say, A, this is going to be a very general product that is not just a thing that developers use.
zh: 所以我认为,对我们来说这是一次重要的练习,用来检查我们的盲点,并认识到:第一,这将是一个非常通用的产品,而不只是开发者使用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: In fact, it is likely that this is most powerful for non-developers.
zh: 事实上,它很可能对非开发者才是最强大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We need to understand that group much better.
zh: 我们需要更好地理解那个群体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then B, is we absolutely live in this kind of Silicon Valley AI bubble, which I think is a useful place to be to kind of push the frontier and push the future of how these products are evolving.
zh: 然后第二,我们绝对生活在这种硅谷 AI 泡沫之中,我认为这对推动前沿、推动这些产品演进的未来来说是一个有用的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we need to actively get out of that because I think a product like this has the chance of really being the way that the mainstream user and the mainstream business customer can interact with AI in a way that's useful.
zh: 但我们需要主动走出这个泡沫,因为我认为像这样的产品有机会真正成为主流用户和主流商业客户以有用的方式与 AI 互动的途径。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's go back to the timelines real quick just to kind of understand that.
zh: 我们快速回到时间线,来了解一下这个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was a month from first line of code to internal beta, and then what happened after that?
zh: 所以从第一行代码到内部测试版是一个月,那之后发生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: It was about three weeks from internal beta to public launch, and then I think we're about three weeks out from public launch as of recording this.
zh: 从内部测试版到公开发布大约三周,然后截至录制这期节目时,我们公开发布大约三周了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a month of building the first thing, three weeks only of iterating, and then it's been only three weeks since launch.
zh: 所以花一个月构建第一个东西,只迭代三周,然后发布至今也才三周。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like it's changed the world from my vantage point.
zh: 从我的角度看,它感觉已经改变了世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: So wow, okay.
zh: 所以,哇,好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What most changed in those, I don't know, in those three weeks of internal beta, let's say?
zh: 在那段时间里——比如说在内部测试版的那三周里,变化最大的是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: We unshipped a lot.
zh: 我们下线了很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish I could have shown you what things looked like maybe two weeks out from launch where I think we'd realized that the core team, we had a lot of experimental features that we wanted to get internal feedback on, which was useful.
zh: 我真希望能给你看看大概距离发布还有两周时的样子,那时我们意识到,核心团队里有很多我们想获得内部反馈的实验性功能,这是有用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also were kind of putting pseudo developery visibility tools into Grok Bot instead of having a separate observability pane for those things.
zh: 我们还把一些伪开发者可见性工具塞进了 Grok Bot,而不是为这些东西单独做一个可观测性面板。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, we actually did expose sometimes a lot of the internal thinking of the models and the specific memories it would store and all of these things, which was useful to debug issues.
zh: 所以举例来说,我们确实暴露过很多时候模型的内部思考、它存储的具体记忆以及所有这些东西,这对调试问题很有用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you're building the product, you didn't want to go somewhere else to maybe pull that context, but we had to really aggressively trim what we think the user absolutely needs to see in the surface versus what they don't.
zh: 而且如果你正在构建这个产品,你不会想去别的地方拉取那些上下文,但我们不得不非常激进地裁剪,弄清楚用户在界面上绝对需要看到什么,以及不需要看到什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's even more room there to run, which is something the team's focused on right now is how can we just ruthlessly simplify this product and abstract away anything the user doesn't need to actively be thinking about?
zh: 我认为那里还有更多可以发挥的空间,这正是团队现在专注的事情:我们如何能无情地简化这个产品,把任何用户不需要主动思考的东西都抽象掉?

speaker: Unknown
en: So that was one big push was unship, a lot of jank.
zh: 所以那是一次大的推动:下线很多粗糙的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think the second big push those few weeks was making it just work.
zh: 然后我认为那几周的第二个大推动是让它就是能用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of what people want from AI is not this thing with lots of dropdown menus and bells and whistles, but just a thing that you describe a task, a task that's meaningful to you, and it goes and it does it and it comes back with complete work or it comes back with something for you to react to and then steer it in its kind of next cycle.
zh: 我认为人们想从 AI 得到的,并不是那种有很多下拉菜单和花哨功能的东西,而只是一个东西:你描述一个任务,一个对你有意义的任务,它就去做了,然后带着完整的工作成果回来,或者带着一些东西回来让你做出反应,然后在它的下一轮循环中引导它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in order to actually deliver on that promise, it's actually not a lot of feature product roadmap style stuff.
zh: 而为了真正兑现这个承诺,其实并不是很多功能性的产品路线图式的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like hill climbing five really important problems in the backend that many users don't directly experience, but you totally feel when your bot is going off and doing something and can't click the right button, or your bot is off and doing something and can't log into a website and it just completely stalls your ability to make progress on that task.
zh: 而更像是攀登后端五个非常重要的问题,许多用户不会直接体验到它们,但当你的智能体出去做某件事却点不到正确的按钮时,或者你的智能体出去做某件事却登录不了某个网站、完全卡住了你在这个任务上取得进展的能力时,你完全能感觉到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so those few weeks we collected a really rich set of what are tasks that people actually are giving bot, how can we quantify these things and how can we see week over week that across those categories of tasks that we're hill climbing on very important dimensions to making that just work behind the scenes?
zh: 所以在那几周里,我们收集了非常丰富的一套数据:人们实际交给智能体的是什么任务,我们如何量化这些事情,以及我们如何逐周看到,在这些类别的任务中,我们正在那些对让它在后台就是能用的非常重要的维度上攀登。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there an example, one of those hills you were climbing that was kind of a technical breakthrough or technical challenge you overcame that really helped it just work?
zh: 有没有这样一个例子,你们攀登的那些山中的一座,是一种技术突破或你们克服的技术挑战,真正帮助它就是能用了?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: One example was from rolling out Grok Bot, one group inside of the company that was actually incredibly bot pilled, so to speak, was our go-to-market team was sales.
zh: 一个例子是推出 Grok Bot 时，公司内部有一个团队可以说真的被 bot 深度种草了，那就是我们的市场团队，也就是销售。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are a bunch of tools that sales uses that do not have well-supported MCPs or APIs.
zh: 销售使用的一系列工具并没有支持良好的 MCP 或 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's a lot of what made bot so before and after powerful for this group was these were things that they just could not give another AI tool reliably.
zh: 我认为这正是 bot 对这个团队前后反差如此强大的主要原因，因为这些是他们的东西根本无法可靠地交给另一个 AI 工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We would get stuck at some part in the process.
zh: 我们总会在流程的某个环节卡住。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Bot kind of felt like they had an assistant or kind of felt like they onboarded someone to their personal team, they gave it a laptop and it could just run.
zh: 而 Bot 给他们的感觉就像是有了一个助理，或者说像是给他们的个人团队招了一个人入职，给了它一台笔记本电脑，它就能直接跑起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there were a bunch of small things and probably a list of 10 or 20 of them of places where for whatever reason, the mouse would just not have fine enough control to click on exactly that part of the Salesforce dashboard or something like that, that we would have to take back to the core team working on really the infrastructure to say, "Here's a very concrete case of where the agent not having this visibility into the browser or this visibility into the pixels on the screen is making it impossible for this task to be done."
zh: 所以有很多小问题，大概列了 10 到 20 个，出于某种原因，鼠标就是没有足够精细的控制力去点击 Salesforce 仪表盘上的那个确切位置之类的，我们不得不把这些反馈给核心团队——真正在做基础设施的团队——说：“这里有一个非常具体的案例，智能体因为无法看到浏览器、无法看到屏幕上的像素，导致这个任务根本无法完成。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was just a lot more tangible than seeing a number on a dashboard slowly creep up.
zh: 这比看着仪表盘上的数字缓慢爬升要具体得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was kind of like new chunks of work getting unlocked and you would immediately feel the feedback where you would ship an improvement that was kind of behind the scenes, kind of infrastructure-y.
zh: 那感觉就像新的大块工作被解锁了，而且你会立刻感受到反馈——你发布了一个幕后性质的、偏基础设施的改进，

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the next day you would just get this outpour of love and appreciation from the sales team that now this workflow that was failing the last seven days finally works.
zh: 然后第二天你就会收到销售团队如潮水般的爱与感激，因为那个过去七天一直失败的工作流终于能用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just a constant exercise of finding those next tasks to unlock and then solving them.
zh: 这就是一个持续的过程：找到下一个要解锁的任务，然后解决它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So computer use basically improvements seems like a big unlock.
zh: 所以计算机使用方面的改进看起来是一个巨大的解锁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard also I had Adam Ward on the podcast who's head of recruiting, head of hiring, basically head of talent.
zh: 我还听说——我也请过 Adam Ward 上播客，他是招聘负责人、录用负责人，基本上是人才负责人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I heard that his team was one of the top users of Grok Bot.
zh: 我听说他的团队是 Grok Bot 的顶级用户之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The recruiting team gave us a lot of great feedback.
zh: 招聘团队给了我们很多很棒的反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anytime the product, especially in the early days, if there was a little bug, we'd get a ping from some folks on the recruiting team.
zh: 尤其在早期，只要产品有一点小 bug，我们就会收到招聘团队某些人的提醒。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think the main use cases for recruiting that were particularly interesting was first, it was incredibly valuable as a sourcing tool.
zh: 对，我认为招聘方面特别有意思的主要用例，首先是它作为搜寻人才工具极其有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one thing Adam talked about on the podcast with you, and it's a big part of our hiring philosophy internally, is looking for a job, being on the market is not a precondition for us trying to hire you.
zh: 我记得 Adam 在和你录播客时提到过一点，也是我们内部招聘理念的重要部分：正在找工作、在市场上流动，并不是我们尝试挖你的前提条件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in a lot of ways, the best way to hire is really just look at the biggest problems at the company that need someone to own it or take it to the next level, find out of the total universe of people in the world who would be best and then ruthlessly go after them and try to convince them to join.
zh: 而且在很多方面，最好的招聘方式其实就是看公司里最大的、需要有人来负责或推上新台阶的问题，从全世界所有人的总集合中找出最合适的人，然后毫不留情地去追他们，努力说服他们加入。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is a lot of the philosophy from the very beginning of the company.
zh: 这是公司从最开始就有的很大一部分理念。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if that's your mindset, really the best recruiting work stream or workflows to automate are not here are a bunch of resumes, read through them, help sort them.
zh: 所以如果你的心态是这样，那么最值得自动化的招聘工作流就不是“这里有一堆简历，读一遍，帮忙排序”。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most useful thing is here's an entire universe of potential people, help match that to this very concrete business problem or this very concrete role that we're recruiting for and help me get in touch with them, help me get coffee with them.
zh: 最有用的是：这里有一个潜在候选人的完整宇宙，帮忙把它匹配到这个非常具体的业务问题或我们正在招的这个非常具体的岗位上，帮我联系上他们，帮我和他们喝杯咖啡。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just throw everything at it.
zh: 我们就把一切都扔给它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there have been some cases of really kind of unexpected ways of finding top talent that is beyond even just looking on LinkedIn and trying to find interesting people.
zh: 所以已经出现了一些以意想不到的方式找到顶尖人才的案例，甚至超越了只是在 LinkedIn 上搜寻有意思的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But who are the co-authors of this paper and the PDF doesn't exist on Google Scholar.
zh: 比如这篇论文的共同作者是谁，而 PDF 在 Google Scholar 上不存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just exists on this conference website.
zh: 它只存在于这个会议的网站上。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want you every morning to go to the conference website, download the PDFs.
zh: 我要你每天早上都去会议网站，下载 PDF。

speaker: Unknown
en: If there are any new ones, you should find every new name that we've not yet tracked.
zh: 如果有新的，你应该找出每一个我们尚未追踪过的新名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should add that name to a spreadsheet, you should do research, you should look at everybody at SpaceXAI, see if there's anyone directly connected.
zh: 你应该把那个名字加进表格，你应该做调研，你应该看看 SpaceXAI 的每一个人，看有没有人直接认识。

speaker: Unknown
en: If so, you should send them a Slack message asking for an introduction.
zh: 如果有，你应该给他们发 Slack 消息请他们做引荐。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's those types of always on sourcing use cases that I think in the past were incredibly manual and now it's the type of thing AI is superhuman at and our team can focus on closing great candidates and getting conversations with great candidates and not pulling these huge lists.
zh: 正是这类全天候的搜寻用例，过去极其依赖人工，而现在它是 AI 拥有超能力的事情，我们的团队可以专注于拿下优秀的候选人、和优秀候选人对话，而不是去拉这些巨大的名单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow, that is such a cool example.
zh: 哇，这真是一个绝妙的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: First of all, someone's about to take the transcript of what you just said, put it into a bot and create their version of this, which is great.
zh: 首先马上就会有人把你刚才说的话做成转录，放进 bot 里，做出他们自己版本的这一套，这很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the other hand, I think you guys could sell a template of this bot for a billion dollars.
zh: 另一方面，我觉得你们可以把这个 bot 的模板卖出十亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think could basically use Adam's team strategy for finding the best people and just turn it into a bot, holy moly, democratizing hiring.
zh: 基本上可以把 Adam 团队寻找最优秀人才的策略做成一个 bot，天哪，这是在让招聘民主化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to come back to a few things.
zh: 我想回到几件事上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is you made this point about unshipping, such a important point I think that people can overlook because AI is not good at telling you what to take out.
zh: 第一是你提到的“撤销上线”(unshipping)，我认为这是一个非常重要却可能被忽视的观点，因为 AI 不擅长告诉你该去掉什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very good at, okay, here's more ideas, here's more stuff.
zh: 它非常擅长的是：好，这里有更多想法，这里有更多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And something that's come up a number of times in the podcast is that's a big space for humans to continue to be very important and valuable is knowing what not to ship and what to cut and what not to do.
zh: 而且播客里多次出现的一个主题是，人类继续保持极其重要和有价值的一大空间，就是知道什么不该上线、该砍掉什么、什么不该做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's so interesting to hear that that's been a big part of the internal evolution from prototype to launches deciding, okay, we need to cut a bunch of stuff.
zh: 所以听到从原型到上线的内部演进中，决定“好，我们需要砍掉一大堆东西”是重要一环，这非常有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything more there?
zh: 这方面还有什么可以补充的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 有。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one thing we talk about internally is for anything that we're working on for Grok Bot, what is the launch post?
zh: 我们内部会讨论的一点是，对于任何我们在为 Grok Bot 做的东西，它的上线公告会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the thing that we would actually tell users?
zh: 我们真正会告诉用户的东西是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's not-
zh: 而如果它不是——

speaker: Unknown
en: A launch tweet, I imagine.
zh: 一条上线推文，我猜。

speaker: Unknown
en: Launch tweet.
zh: 上线推文。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's not compelling, maybe we shouldn't be working on it if it's not something that users will directly feel in the product.
zh: 而如果它不吸引人，也许我们就不该做它，如果它不是用户能在产品里直接感受到的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to take that even one step further, I think there's this old school software tendency to say things like Grok Bot now has, and when you think of completing that sentence, it would be like a new button to press or it'd be a new dropdown or it'd be a new integration that you can press plus and add.
zh: 再进一步说，我认为有一种老派的软件倾向，会说类似“Grok Bot 现在有了”，而当你想着怎么补全这个句子时，它会是一个新的可按的按钮，或者一个新的下拉菜单，或者一个新的集成——按一下加号就能添加的那种。

speaker: Unknown
en: And instead to reframe it as Grok Bot can now, which is I think a much more human way of describing these capabilities.
zh: 而是把它重新表述为“Grok Bot 现在可以……”,我认为这是一种更贴近人的方式来描述这些能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's forced us to think more in the frame of what are tools and what are capabilities that we can give Grok Bot, not what are new things we can add to the product?
zh: 我认为这迫使我们更多地从“我们能给 Grok Bot 哪些工具、哪些能力”的角度思考,而不是“我们能往产品里加什么新东西”。

speaker: Unknown
en: Adding things to the product is not the goal, that's not the thing that's going to push this product forward and make it more useful to more people.
zh: 往产品里加东西不是目标,那不是能推动这个产品前进、让它对更多人更有用的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Making your bots reliably do really impactful work for you behind the scenes in a way that just works and giving them the capabilities to do that, that's what users actually care about.
zh: 让你的机器人可靠地在幕后为你做真正有影响的工作,而且开箱即用,并赋予它们做到这一点的能力——这才是用户真正在意的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think in the context of unshipping, there have been a lot of Grok Bot now has things that we've realized are actually just capabilities that don't need pixels.
zh: 所以我认为,在“下架”的语境下,有很多情况是:Grok Bot 现在有的这些东西,我们意识到其实只是不需要像素的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's kill as many pixels as we can.
zh: 让我们尽可能多地砍掉像素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those can just be things that your bot manipulates behind the scenes for you and you don't need to directly control.
zh: 那些东西可以是你的机器人在幕后替你操作的,你不需要直接控制的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one example of this is the way that many of our competitors, you set up automations or routines is you go into a sidebar, you press plus, you select what the trigger event is, you then select what action it should take after that, and you might describe it in natural language and it's just really clunky.
zh: 我认为这方面的一个例子是,我们的很多竞品设置自动化或例程的方式是:你进入侧边栏,按加号,选择触发事件是什么,然后选择之后应该执行什么动作,你可能用自然语言描述一下,总之非常笨拙。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it means that people don't set up many automations for many things.
zh: 这意味着人们不会为很多事情设置很多自动化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We certainly have seen this in the coding realm.
zh: 我们在编程领域肯定见过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think what Grok Bot did in response to that was actually you should just define automations in natural language and you should tell your bot, "Remind me that at 8:00 AM every day, please."
zh: 所以我认为 Grok Bot 对此的回应是:你应该直接用自然语言定义自动化,你应该告诉你的机器人,“请提醒我每天早上 8 点。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it should just do it and you should never ever have to see that interface of creating an automation.
zh: 然后它就应该照做,而你应该永远不必看到那个创建自动化的界面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's kind of the decision that we've made and now that's how 99% of automations on the platform built.
zh: 所以这差不多就是我们做的决定,现在平台上 99% 的自动化都是这样构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there are a bunch of other places where we can do things like that.
zh: 我认为还有很多其他地方我们可以做类似的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I tweeted about how much I love Grok Bot when it launched and a lot of people replied, they're like, "Wait, can't you just do all this with Codex and Cowork?"
zh: 我在 Grok Bot 发布时发推说我有多喜欢它,很多人回复说,“等等,这些你不是用 Codex 和 Cowork 都能做到吗?”

speaker: Unknown
en: And you can.
zh: 确实可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: Technically everything, as far as I know, you can do with Grok Bot you can do with the other foundational models, the coding assistants.
zh: 据我所知,凡是 Grok Bot 能做的,技术上用其他基础模型、编程助手都能做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me just ask you this big question.
zh: 那么让我问你个大问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it that you think you did that is so different, that made Grok Bot so successful?
zh: 你认为你们做了什么如此不同的事,让 Grok Bot 如此成功?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it was two early decisions that at the time definitely did not feel obvious, but in hindsight, I think are critical to what makes Grok Bot work for people.
zh: 我认为是有两个早期的决定,在当时绝对不觉得显而易见,但事后来看,我认为它们对 Grok Bot 能为人们所用至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the first is you should never have to think about local and cloud and where are these workflows running?
zh: 第一个是:你应该永远不必考虑本地和云、这些工作流在哪里运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does my computer have to be awake?
zh: 我的电脑必须一直开着吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: If I kick it off from my phone, does it need to be tethered to my computer back at home?
zh: 如果我从手机上启动它,它是否需要绑在家里那台电脑上?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's so much jank happening right now when people are trying to conceptualize where this runtime lives.
zh: 现在人们在试图理解这个运行时存在于何处时,有太多别扭的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we made a really early decision that this should just all be in the cloud.
zh: 而我们很早就做了一个决定:这一切就都应该在云端。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it's in the cloud and it's this persistent colleague that has its own computer, it can do its own work, it has the same state everywhere you interact with it opens up a lot of really amazing opportunities to text your bot, kick it off from your phone.
zh: 如果它在云端,而且是一个拥有自己电脑的持久同事,它能做自己的工作,它在任何你与它交互的地方都有相同的状态,这就打开了很多非常棒的机会:你可以给机器人发消息,从手机上启动它。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the future, you should be able to call your bot from anywhere and it should be able to do real work.This is its own entity and it lives separately from your device.
zh: 将来,你应该能从任何地方呼叫你的机器人,它应该能做真正的工作。它是独立的实体,独立于你的设备存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that was a very important decision that current products I think haven't made that same decision.
zh: 我认为这是一个非常重要的决定,而现有的产品我认为没有做出同样的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it has a bunch of paper cuts as a result of it that users feel every day.
zh: 我认为正因如此,它们有一堆让用户每天都能感受到的小别扭。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the second decision was to take that one step further of not only should this be an agent loop that kind of runs in the cloud and you can interact with in various ways, it's actually really important that these bots have their own computer.
zh: 我认为第二个决定是把那一步再往前推:不仅是这是一个在云端运行、你可以以各种方式与之交互的智能体循环,而且这些机器人拥有自己的电脑非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of it is what I described earlier of there are a bunch of tasks that don't have well-supported MCPs and APIs.
zh: 部分原因是我之前描述的:有很多任务没有支持良好的 MCP 和 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: We as humans don't do our jobs via MCPs and APIs.
zh: 我们人类不是通过 MCP 和 API 来做工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We use a computer and we click on pixels and we kind of type things and input boxes and it's very important that your bot has those baseline capabilities as well.
zh: 我们用电脑,点击像素,在输入框里打字输入,你的机器人也具备这些基线能力非常重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even to go one step further, I think we're in a really weird moment right now that I think we're going to look back on and be like, I'm surprised that this is the way that a lot of people worked with AI, where you're onboarding these super intelligent new colleagues, these AI bots, and you're asking them to share the same computer that you have.
zh: 但再往前说一步,我认为我们现在正处于一个非常奇怪的时刻,将来回头看我们会说:我很惊讶很多人就是这样与 AI 一起工作的——你在给这些超级智能的新同事、这些 AI 机器人做入职培训,却让它们和你共用同一台电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's crazy.
zh: 这太疯狂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you were onboarding someone to your team and you said, "It's your first day, I'm going to onboard you.
zh: 如果你给团队里的新人做入职培训,你说:“今天是你第一天,我来给你做入职。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have your own laptop, you're going to sit next to me, we're going to share this laptop forever and constantly trip over each other.
zh: 你没有自己的笔记本,你要坐在我旁边,我们要永远共用这台笔记本,不断互相绊倒。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're going to have access to my credentials, I'm going to have access to your credentials."
zh: 你能访问我的凭证,我也能访问你的凭证。”

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a good reason why that's not the way people operate.
zh: 人们不这样运作是有充分理由的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think bots and these kind of AI colleagues of the future will also need a way to onboard them that's somewhat similar and we've tried to push the product in that direction.
zh: 我认为机器人和未来的这类 AI 同事也需要一种有些类似的入职方式,我们一直试图把产品往这个方向推。

speaker: Unknown
en: That is so funny.
zh: 这太有意思了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think the other companies didn't do this?
zh: 你觉得为什么其他公司没有这么做?

speaker: Unknown
en: My guess is they were building off of their existing coding assistant platform and approach, and this was a pretty big shift.
zh: 我的猜测是,它们是在现有的编程助手平台和方法之上构建的,而这是一个相当大的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of it comes down to starting from scratch and how freeing that is.
zh: 我认为很大程度上归结于从零开始,以及那有多自由。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we felt that ourselves where a lot of the primitives in Grok Bot we had attempted or we had built in other ways, cloud infrastructure we built for coding agents.
zh: 我们自己也体会到了这一点:Grok Bot 的很多基元我们都曾尝试过,或曾用其他方式构建过——我们为编程智能体构建的云基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that you could maybe name agents and talk to them as discrete entities, it's a pattern that we're also seeing for developers bringing specific named agents into Slack.
zh: 你可以给智能体命名并把它们当作离散实体来交谈的方式,这也是我们看到开发者把特定的命名智能体引入 Slack 的一种模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But instead of trying to retrofit those concepts into some new surface or into an existing surface, which I think would've been the strong default I think for many companies, we decided to start from scratch and we decided to just try to get these things really right for general knowledge work, which is a new audience.
zh: 但我们没有试图把这些概念改造进某个新界面或现有界面——我认为对很多公司来说那会是强烈的默认选择——我们决定从零开始,我们决定把这些东西真正为通用知识工作做好,而这是一个新的受众。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then second, for the point in time that we're at now where the models are very capable and if you give them the right tools and the right infrastructure, they can do a lot.
zh: 其次,对于我们现在所处的时间点,模型能力已经很强,如果你给它们合适的工具和合适的基础设施,它们能做很多事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a lot of these ideas, these aren't strokes of genius on our part and I think for good reason.
zh: 但这些想法并不是我们的天才之举,而且我认为这是有道理的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think these are primitives that had already been getting attention and product market fit by other products, the open claws of the world.
zh: 我认为这些是已经被其他产品、open claws 这类产品获得关注并找到产品市场契合度的基元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we took a lot of inspiration from that and tried to productize it into a bit of a tighter surface, something that required a little bit less setup and I think it was more accessible to more people.
zh: 我认为我们从中学到了很多灵感，并试图把它产品化成一个更紧凑的界面，一个需要更少设置的东西，我认为它对更多人来说更容易上手。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think our competitors and other tools that have been trying to solve these types of problems, I think we're all seeing the same opportunity.
zh: 所以我认为我们的竞争对手和其他一直试图解决这类问题的工具，我认为我们都在看到同样的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're seeing a lot of the feedback from the market, but I think it's just been hard to act on if you're stuck in the existing paradigm.
zh: 我认为我们从市场中看到了很多反馈，但我认为如果你被困在现有的范式中，就很难据此采取行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you have a lot of sunk cost in that existing paradigm, it's very painful to create a new thing from scratch.
zh: 而如果你在现有范式中投入了大量沉没成本，从零开始创造一个新东西是非常痛苦的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think a lot of that is what allowed the product to just work and click for so many people.
zh: 我认为很多这些因素正是让这个产品对这么多人来说直接可用、立刻产生共鸣的原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I'm hearing here is the keys to success of what made this breakout a cloud-based computer for every bot instead of locally, a name kind of specific bot.
zh: 所以我在这里听到的是，让这个产品爆火的关键在于：为每个 bot 提供一台基于云的计算机，而不是本地的，一种针对特定任务的 bot，名字也有点具体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, there's this, we're all moving from agents to bots now.
zh: 顺便说一句，现在我们都在从 agents 转向 bots 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nice job.
zh: 干得漂亮。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like you guys have pushed it over and now, okay, we're all bots now.
zh: 感觉你们已经把它推过去了，现在，好了，我们全都是 bots 了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So a bot per kind of task use case, very unique versus a thread conversation or something or a one-off job.
zh: 所以是每个任务、每个用例对应一个 bot，非常独特，区别于一个线程对话或者一个一次性的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it feels like it just works, was a core part of this.
zh: 然后感觉「它直接就能用」是这件事的核心部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you talked about how long it took to get to that place of like, okay, now it actually works really well.
zh: 而且你谈到了花了多长时间才达到那个「好吧，现在它真的很好用了」的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned OpenClaw.
zh: 你提到了 OpenClaw。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously this is inspired by that, which to me, when I first used OpenClaw, like, holy, this is the future.
zh: 显然这是受它启发的，而对我来说，我第一次用 OpenClaw 的时候，就像，天哪，这就是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: How could we not have this?
zh: 我们怎么能没有这个东西呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then Hermes came out and everyone's been trying to build the OpenClaw that works very easily for everybody.
zh: 然后 Hermes 出来了，所有人都在试图构建一个对每个人都非常容易好用的 OpenClaw。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you say more about just how OpenClaw and that story informed the way you guys thought about it?
zh: 你能再多说说 OpenClaw 和那段故事是如何影响你们的思考方式的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think OpenClaw got two major things right that when we were seeing the way the market was reacting to OpenClaw and ourselves using the product, we found quite exciting.
zh: 是的，我认为 OpenClaw 做对了两件大事，当我们观察市场对 OpenClaw 的反应以及我们自己使用这个产品时，我们觉得非常令人兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the first thing was the models are really smart and they're going to continue to get smarter, but even at current capability levels, if you can just give your bot access to the tools that you use to do your job, it can get a lot of the way there.
zh: 我认为第一件事是，模型真的很聪明，而且它们会继续变得更聪明，但即使在当前的能力水平上，如果你只是让你的 bot 能访问你用来完成工作的那些工具，它就能走完大部分的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a lot of the places where people think AI is dumb or maybe not as impactful as it's been promised, a lot of that I think is downstream of it just being harnessed in the wrong way.
zh: 在很多人们认为 AI 很笨、或者可能没有承诺的那么有影响力的地方，我认为很多情况都是它只是被错误地使用方式所拖累的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if you give access to a much larger set of things, if it has access to its own computer, how far can you go?
zh: 所以如果你给它访问一个大得多的东西集合，如果它能访问自己的计算机，你能走多远？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think OpenClaw really forced that question for many people.
zh: 我认为 OpenClaw 真的把这个问题抛给了很多人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think the second way OpenClaw changed the mental model of AI was really viewing these things much more as colleagues and teammates and people and personifying it a bit more and it being this helper entity that has access to your life and can extend you even further.
zh: 然后我认为 OpenClaw 改变人们对 AI 心智模型的第二种方式，是真的把这些东西更多地看作同事、队友和人，更多地把它人格化，让它成为一个能访问你的生活、能把你进一步延伸的助手实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we took a lot of that and I think what Grok Bot maybe extended was, A, it needs to be really easy to set up and the hacky, you have a VPN at home and a Mac mini set up, clearly it was not going to scale to millions of users.
zh: 所以我们吸收了很多这些，而我认为 Grok Bot 可能延伸的是：第一，它必须非常容易设置，那种 hacky 的方式——你家里有一个 VPN 和一台 Mac mini 的设置，显然是无法扩展到数百万用户的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly it's not going to be the way importantly that businesses take advantage of this technology.
zh: 显然，重要的是，它也不会成为企业利用这项技术的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we really wanted to build an amazing product with that in mind.
zh: 所以我们真的想以此为目标打造一个出色的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then second is I think there are a lot of places, a lot of rough edges to stand down and just make a delightful product experience and make these things just work and try to remove some of the abstractions that power users of AI are very familiar with, things like skills, for example.
zh: 然后第二点是，我认为还有很多地方、很多粗糙的边缘需要打磨掉，去打造一个令人愉悦的产品体验，让这些东西直接就能用，并试图移除一些 AI 高级用户非常熟悉的抽象，比如 skills 之类的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: How can we make a Grok Bot user not even have to know what a skill is?
zh: 我们怎么能让一个 Grok Bot 用户甚至不需要知道什么是 skill？

speaker: Unknown
en: They should never have to type a slash command.
zh: 他们永远不需要输入斜杠命令。

speaker: Unknown
en: These things should be created in the background as a useful primitive that the bots have access to, but something that users, it's not incumbent on them to always be on the cutting edge of AI.
zh: 这些东西应该在后台被创建，作为 bots 可以使用的有用原语，但对用户来说，并不要求他们必须始终站在 AI 的最前沿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that's really where we tried to innovate and I think there's still more room to go there.
zh: 所以这就是我们真正试图创新的地方，我认为在这方面还有更多的空间可以挖掘。

speaker: Unknown
en: As you say that, I have my Mac mini with my formerly live OpenClaw on there and that was an era and it's so awesome the work that it has inspired.
zh: 你这么说的时候，我想起我的 Mac mini 上还跑着我以前活跃的 OpenClaw，那是一个时代，它所启发的这些工作太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know it continues.
zh: 我知道它还在继续。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know there's still a lot of value to OpenClaw, but when I saw Claire Vo, who's been the biggest proponent of Open Claw and it's become a core part of the way she lives and works with her kids and does all her work, she just switched all over OpenClaws.
zh: 我知道 OpenClaw 仍然有很多价值，但当我看到 Claire Vo——她一直是 OpenClaw 最大的支持者，它已经成为她和孩子们一起生活、做她所有工作的方式的核心部分——她全面切换到了 OpenClaws。

speaker: Unknown
en: She shut them all down and switched to Grok Bot.
zh: 她把它们全部关掉，切换到了 Grok Bot。

speaker: Unknown
en: It sounds funny, but that's actually a huge milestone of just how much things have shifted.
zh: 这听起来有点好笑，但这其实是一个巨大的里程碑，说明事情已经发生了多大的转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the vision for Grok Bot?
zh: Grok Bot 的愿景是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where does this go?
zh: 它会走向哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does this look like in the future?
zh: 未来它会是什么样子？

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the ideal platonic version of Grok Bot?
zh: Grok Bot 理想的柏拉图式版本是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: The ultimate vision of Grok Bot is incredibly simple, which is you should have a team of AI bots that help you with your job and help you with your life.
zh: Grok Bot 的终极愿景非常简单，那就是你应该拥有一支 AI bot 团队，帮助你完成工作，也帮助你打理生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it should really feel like a team.
zh: 而且它应该真的感觉像一个团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should really feel like teammates that are autonomous are helping you.
zh: 它应该真的感觉像是有自主能力的队友在帮助你。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can steer them in various ways.
zh: 你可以用各种方式引导他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't have to micromanage them.
zh: 你不需要对他们进行微管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have access to the tools necessary to do great ambitious work.
zh: 他们有权访问完成伟大的、有雄心的工作所需的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing we really use as a north star on the product side in building this is as we kind of get closer to this teammate future, how can we, in every product decision we make, think about this less from the perspective of a SaaS product and more from the perspective of we're trying to build useful AI teammates.
zh: 而在打造这个产品的过程中，我们真正用作北极星的一点是：随着我们越来越接近这个队友式的未来，我们如何在做的每一个产品决策中，少从 SaaS 产品的角度去思考，多从「我们是在努力打造有用的 AI 队友」的角度去思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there have been a bunch of examples where we kind of have to push ourselves to be more like colleague pilled in a way.
zh: 所以有很多例子，我们不得不推着自己变得更像「同事脑」一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: We sometimes use that term where we're having a product debate about something, there are good arguments on one side, there are good arguments on another side, both paths feel sensible.
zh: 我们有时会用这个词，当我们进行一场关于某件事的产品辩论时，一方有好论点，另一方也有好论点，两条路都感觉合理。

speaker: Unknown
en: In product land, this maybe doesn't feel like there's a clear cut answer.
zh: 在产品领域，这可能不觉得有一个明确无疑的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you zoom out a little bit and you remove yourself from the tech company-ness of it all and you start thinking, how would a human do this?
zh: 然后你稍微跳出来一点,把自己从中那股科技公司味儿里抽离出来,开始想:一个人会怎么做这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: What would you want from your teammate in this exact situation?
zh: 在这个确切的情境下,你会希望你的队友为你做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And oftentimes the answer is really clarifying and pretty unanimous.
zh: 而答案往往非常清晰,而且相当一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's oftentimes not a lot of disagreement among the room of how a human teammate you would prefer to work with in a certain way.
zh: 对于你更愿意以某种方式共事的人类队友是怎样的,房间里往往没有太多分歧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once that answer is there, well then we just need to build it and there are product implications, there are model implications, there's a lot of things that need to go right to actually deliver on that experience.
zh: 一旦答案有了,那我们就只需要把它构建出来,这有产品层面的影响,有模型层面的影响,要真正交付那种体验,有很多事情需要做对。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in some ways it's not a rocket science, doesn't require you being a genius.
zh: 但从某种意义上说,这并不是火箭科学,不需要你是个天才。

speaker: Unknown
en: You just need to ask the question of what would you want from a human teammate and can we push AI to behave in a similar way?
zh: 你只需要问这个问题:你会希望从一个人类队友那里得到什么,我们能否推动 AI 以类似的方式表现?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so to give some examples of that, we've been thinking about what the right voice experience with these bots should be.
zh: 举一些例子来说明这一点,我们一直在思考与这些机器人之间正确的语音体验应该是什么样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think in the context of a human, for example, we have a really good analog of a lot of times I'm slacking back and forth with a teammate, we're sharing context, and a lot of times it's just much simpler to get on a five-minute huddle with them and just press huddle, talk back and forth.
zh: ——更正:[[358]] 而我认为,以人类的语境来说,举个例子,我们有一个很好的类比:很多时候我在和队友用 Slack 来回沟通,我们在共享上下文,而很多时候,更简单的做法是直接和他们开一个五分钟的临时会议,按一下 huddle,来回聊。

speaker: Unknown
en: I share my screen, I show exactly what's on my mind, they share their screen, we hop off, and then we continue async from there.
zh: 我共享屏幕,展示我脑子里到底在想什么,他们共享他们的屏幕,然后我们挂断,之后从那里继续异步协作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's not really an experience that any AI product has gotten right right now, and it is deeply integral to the way that I think humans collaborate.
zh: 而这并不是当下任何 AI 产品真正做对了的体验,但它是人类协作方式中极为核心的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we want to build something like that.
zh: 所以我们想构建类似这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are a bunch of other examples of these very clear patterns that just work that I think you should also feel when working with AI.
zh: 还有很多其他这样显而易见、就是有效的模式的例子,我认为你在与 AI 共事时也应该能感受到它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this term colleague build, and it's come up so many times over the course of this chat already how that is kind of a through line to making these decisions.
zh: 我很喜欢「同事构建」这个词,在这次对话中它已经被提到过很多次了,它是做出这些决策的一条主线。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, the computer example you gave is so good.
zh: 例如,你举的电脑的例子就非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously people would have their own computer.
zh: 显然人们会拥有自己的电脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: The naming piece is also very important part of that.
zh: 命名这块也是其中非常重要的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: A big question on my mind in this space, and I'm so curious to get your take, is the separation between work and personal.
zh: 我在这个领域心里最大的一个问题,而且我非常想听听你的看法,是工作与个人之间的分离。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think people will have two different assistants, a work and a personal, or do you think it'll be one?
zh: 你认为人们会有两个不同的助手,一个工作用、一个个人用,还是只有一个?

speaker: Unknown
en: When people think about a work product versus a consumer product, I think there's just a lot of baggage that comes from the last decade or two of horrible B2B software that leads to people seeing a product that is very simple.
zh: 当人们思考工作产品与消费级产品时,我认为过去一二十年糟糕的 B2B 软件带来了很多包袱,导致人们看到一个非常简单的产品时。

speaker: Unknown
en: In some ways ChatGPT was like this.
zh: 某种程度上 ChatGPT 就是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Grok Bot has many of these properties.
zh: 我觉得 Grok Bot 有很多这样的特性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And assuming that it's not a work product or assuming that it's not a power tool.
zh: 就假定它不是一个工作产品,或者假定它不是一个强力工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you think of a power tool in this kind of last generation, I, in my head, picture something a bit like Photoshop, for example, where there are all of these different dials to turn very precisely.
zh: 而当你想到上一代意义上的强力工具,我脑海里会浮现出类似 Photoshop 的东西,那里有各种各样可以非常精确调节的旋钮。

speaker: Unknown
en: The user of the tool is this kind of ultimate cockpit flyer who knows exactly what all the knobs do and can use them perfectly.
zh: 工具的用户是那种终极的驾驶舱飞行员,确切知道每个旋钮是干什么的,并且能完美地使用它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think power tools of the future will actually be very different from that, where it is mostly just intent being expressed and good steering on the part of the human and these AI tools abstract away all of the knobs.
zh: 而我认为未来的强力工具实际上会与此非常不同:主要是表达意图,加上人类良好的引导,这些 AI 工具把所有旋钮都抽象掉了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should never see them unless you need to directly manipulate it, which might happen and there should be a great affordance for that.
zh: 你根本不该看到它们,除非你需要直接操作,这种情况可能发生,而且应该为此提供很好的可操作性。

speaker: Unknown
en: But ultimately, it really is just working with a teammate.
zh: 但归根结底,它真的就是在和一位队友共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the interface for that is quite conversational.
zh: 因此它的界面是相当对话式的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so in a lot of ways, Grok Bot, when you look at it, when I walk by someone's desk and I see Grok Bot up on their computer, for me for a split second, I'm like, "Oh, are they on a messaging app?"
zh: 所以在很多方面,当你看 Grok Bot——当我走过某人的工位,看到他们电脑上开着 Grok Bot 时,有那么一瞬间我会想:「哦,他们是在用即时通讯软件吗?」

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's like, no, this is actually the primary tool that they're using to do much of their work.
zh: 然后发现,不,这其实是他们用来完成大部分工作的主要工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think to your question of are you going to have a different set of bots for your personal life and a different set of bots for your work life.
zh: 所以回到你的问题:你的个人生活会不会有一套不同的机器人,工作生活又有一套不同的机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think there will be a separation for many people.
zh: 我确实认为对很多人来说会有分离。

speaker: Unknown
en: They want a separation between personal and work life, and I think that's great.
zh: 他们想要个人生活与工作生活之间的分离,我觉得这很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's important.
zh: 我认为这很重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there are a lot of common sense reasons why those things should be separate, even from the perspective of an enterprise.
zh: 而且我认为,即便从企业的角度看,也有很多常识性的理由说明这些东西应该分开。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think our goal and the thing we're trying to build towards is Grok Bot should be the way that a large portion of the things you do day-to-day in your work, you should be able to delegate a lot of that to Grok Bot and focus on the higher leverage things.
zh: 但我认为我们的目标、我们试图构建的方向是:你日常工作中很大一部分事情,应该能够大量委托给 Grok Bot,从而专注于更高杠杆的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it should similarly be the way that you delegate a lot of the low leverage parts of your personal life.
zh: 同样,它也应该成为你委托个人生活中大量低杠杆事务的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those two things actually are not different problem sets.
zh: 而这两件事实际上并不是不同的问题集合。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a lot of ways, the product form factor and the ways of solving those problems is pretty much the same.
zh: 在很多方面,这两者的产品形态和解决问题的方法几乎是相同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so my instinct is that I think one product will be the best form factor for both of those things, and that's really what we want to build.
zh: 所以我的直觉是,我认为一个产品将是同时满足这两件事的最佳形态,而这也正是我们真正想要构建的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Bam, that's a big TAM right there.
zh: 啪,这可是一个巨大的 TAM。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love to hear.
zh: 我很乐意听到这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes so much sense.
zh: 这非常说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously the question is how do you avoid cross-contamination, personal stuff somehow infiltrating, ex-filtrating stuff from work, but it feels like that's kind of okay.
zh: 显然问题是如何避免交叉污染,个人内容不知怎么渗透进来、工作内容外泄出去,但感觉这某种程度上还行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I'm hearing is that's the direction.
zh: 所以我听到的是,这就是方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is just how to do that and make people feel super safe, have the SOC 2 stuff in place and also just feel really fun.
zh: 问题只是如何做到这一点,并让人们感到非常安全,把 SOC 2 之类的合规准备好,同时也让人感觉真的很有趣。

zh: 本期节目由 Mercury 为您呈现,彻底不同的银行服务,现在还带 Spend。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've been a Mercury customer for so many years now.
zh: 我当 Mercury 的客户已经很多年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I switched all my business banking to Mercury, and honestly, I could not be happier.
zh: 我把我所有的商业银行业务都切换到了 Mercury,说实话,我开心得不能再开心了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's what online banking feels like when it's built by product people, not by bankers.
zh: 这就像是由产品人员而不是银行家构建的网上银行的感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now with Spend, you can give your team individual cards, set spending limits per person or per team, and have expense receipts automatically pulled in from Gmail or over text.
zh: 现在有了 Spend,你可以给团队每个人单独的卡片,为每个人或每个团队设置消费限额,并让费用收据自动从 Gmail 或短信中拉取进来。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can even give your AI agents their own cards with their own limits and policies.
zh: 你甚至可以给你的 AI 智能体它们自己的卡片,带有它们自己的限额和策略。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most founders start out the same way, one card used by everybody at the company.
zh: 大多数创始人的起步方式都是一样的,一张卡片全公司所有人共用。

speaker: Unknown
en: It works until it stops working.
zh: 它能一直用,直到用不了的那天。

speaker: Unknown
en: Someone goes over, a receipt disappears.
zh: 有人超支了,一张收据不见了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You spend two days trying to figure out who spent what and why.
zh: 你花两天时间试图弄清楚谁花了什么、为什么花。

en: Spend is expense management built directly into Mercury.
zh: Spend 是直接内置于 Mercury 的费用管理。

speaker: Unknown
en: All your team's cards, budgets, and reimbursements all live in the same place as your business banking.
zh: 你团队所有的卡片、预算和报销都和你的商业银行业务在同一个地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: No chasing, no manual reviews, no end of month scramble.
zh: 不用追着要,不用人工审核,不用月底手忙脚乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: The result is a team that can move fast in a founder who is no longer the bottleneck.
zh: 结果就是一个可以快速行动的团队,以及一个不再是瓶颈的创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Learn more and get signed up at mercury.com.
zh: 到 mercury.com 了解更多并注册。

zh: Mercury 是一家金融科技公司,不是 FDIC 承保的银行。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me ask you a couple technical questions.
zh: 让我问你几个技术问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the computer side, what's the simplest way to think about what you get as a part of your Grok Bot account?
zh: 在计算机这块,理解你的 Grok Bot 账户能获得什么,最简单的方式是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it like AVM that is running in the cloud with multiple logins?
zh: 是像一个在云端运行、支持多个登录的 VM 吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it a separate VM instance per bot?
zh: 还是每个 bot 一个单独的 VM 实例?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we understand that as much as you can share?
zh: 在你尽可能分享的范围内,我们该怎么理解它?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think to go back to the teammate frame of the product, to extend the analogy even further, if we were on a team together, you and me, I think the number of times that you would have to manually take over my computer and start clicking on things and you're doing this wrong, you should go here instead and type in manually, hopefully it's pretty close to zero.
zh: 是的,我想回到产品的队友框架,进一步延伸这个类比,如果我们俩在一个团队里,你和我,我想你需要手动接管我的电脑、开始点来点去、说你做错了、你应该到这里来然后手动输入,这种情况的次数,希望是非常接近零的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hopefully that is not something you have to really do with a colleague or a teammate.
zh: 希望这不是你真的需要对一个同事或队友做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so similarly, I think right now we're in a place where computer use is good, it's getting much better, and in very short order, I think the computer concept will be completely abstracted away from the user.
zh: 所以类似地,我想我们现在所处的位置是,计算机使用已经不错了,它正在变得好得多,而且在很短的时间内,我认为计算机这个概念将会完全从用户那里被抽象掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should never be clicking into a remote virtual machine.
zh: 你应该永远不需要点进一个远程虚拟机。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should never have to take control if there's a wasteful path and you have to steer it into the correct path.
zh: 如果有一条浪费的路径,你应该永远不需要接管控制并把它引导到正确的路径上。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in the medium term, I think the computer concept will be an important concept for users to have, but will not actually be something that they're interacting with.
zh: 所以在中期,我认为计算机这个概念对用户来说会是一个重要的概念,但实际不会是他们与之交互的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the right way of thinking about Grok Bot is it's a team of bots, it's a team of agents that do work for you.
zh: 所以我认为理解 Grok Bot 的正确方式是,它是一个 bot 团队,一个为你工作的智能体团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in terms of what they have access to, they have access to a very long memory set of your past interactions with them.
zh: 至于它们能访问什么,它们可以访问一个很长的记忆集合,记录着你与它们的过去交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think there's a current paradigm if you create a new chat for each discrete unit of work, I think there are a lot of problems with that.
zh: 所以我认为现在有一个范式,就是为每个离散的工作单元创建一个新聊天,我认为这有很多问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I find myself copying and pasting between chats all the time.
zh: 我发现自己总是在聊天之间复制粘贴。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's just not a great way of grouping categories of work.
zh: 我觉得这不是给工作类别分组的好方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead, the same way on a team, you have a good way of grouping categories of work of roles.
zh: 相反,就像在一个团队里,你有一个对工作类别、角色分组的好方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should have roles of different swim lanes of work that you do, and it should learn from you and it should get smarter over time.
zh: 你应该有不同泳道的角色,它应该向你学习,并且随着时间变得更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that's one very critical thing is these are long-lived agents.
zh: 所以我认为这是一个非常关键的地方:这些是长生命周期的智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are not individual one-off sessions, and these agents get smarter over time.
zh: 这些不是一次性的单独会话,而且这些智能体会随着时间变得更聪明。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the second thing is those agents have access to all of the tools that you would expect a human colleague to have, which is the APIs, the MCPs, that's great, but then access to its own computer, which it can freely manipulate the way that you would.
zh: 然后第二件事是,那些智能体可以访问你期望一个人类同事拥有的所有工具,也就是 API、MCP,这些很棒,但还有对它自己计算机的访问权,它可以像你一样自由地操作它。

speaker: Unknown
en: At this meetup that I went to, Shab, who's on the, I think, go to market team, demoed something that blew everyone's mind.
zh: 在我参加的那个聚会上,Shab,他好像在市场推广团队,演示了一个让所有人都惊掉下巴的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you have a computer within each agent, you can run a lot of different things on the computer.
zh: 因为每个智能体内部都有一台计算机,你可以在那台计算机上运行很多不同的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was running Grok Bot within Grok Bot.
zh: 他在 Grok Bot 里运行 Grok Bot。

speaker: Unknown
en: The bot can run its own Grok Bots, and I know he was using it for testing and watching regressions and things like that, but that's just a mind-expanding idea.
zh: bot 可以运行它自己的 Grok Bot,我知道他是在用它做测试、观察回归之类的事情,但这真是一个让人脑洞大开的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm curious how many levels you can go before the universe collapses on itself.
zh: 我很好奇你能套多少层,直到宇宙自我坍缩。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do that one too.
zh: 我也做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: That one's actually a very useful thing to do is you download Grok Bot for one of your bots, mine is like a QA tester bot.
zh: 那个其实是一件非常有用的事情,就是为你其中一个 bot 下载 Grok Bot,我的是一个类似 QA 测试员的 bot。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that way if there's ever bug report or if we're testing out a new build, for example, of the desktop app, I can just say, "Hey, here are 10 workflows that we need to make sure are getting better release after release.
zh: 这样一来,如果有 bug 报告,或者比如我们在测试桌面应用的新构建版本,我就可以说:"嘿,这里有 10 个工作流,我们需要确保它们一次又一次的发布中变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want you to test it.
zh: 我要你测试它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want you to write it to this notion document that has an extensive list of all of the past tests that we've done of past client versions and compare them."
zh: 我要你把它写到这份 notion 文档里,里面有一份我们过去对所有过往客户端版本所做测试的详尽清单,并进行比较。"

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think once you start breaking out of this is AI chat with a set of connections, which is I think where most people are conceptually now, instead to this is a colleague with a computer and anything I would ask a colleague to do on a computer, I can ask Grok Bot to do.
zh: 所以我认为,一旦你开始跳出「这是带一组连接的 AI 聊天」这个大多数人现在概念上的认知,转向「这是一个拥有计算机的同事,任何我会请同事在计算机上做的事,我都可以请 Grok Bot 做」。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just raises the ceiling, I think, of what you would think to give to AI.
zh: 我认为这提高了你想到交给 AI 的事情的天花板。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are there any other mind-expanding use cases or ways to use Grok Bot that you've seen or you use?
zh: 你还见过或使用过其他脑洞大开的 Grok Bot 用例或用法吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: One pattern that I've seen from many users that is simple, but I think there's a lot of depth if you keep investing in making it better, and this is where I can get kind of nerdy about optimizing my setup, is Grok Bot as an infovore in some ways of just consuming huge quantities of information, removing that from your own cognitive load, giving you peace, and then coming to you with the stuff that's important.
zh: 我从很多用户身上见过的一个模式,它很简单,但如果你持续投入把它做得更好,我认为有很深的潜力——这也是我会变得有点极客、优化我自己设置的地方——就是把 Grok Bot 当作某种意义上的信息吞噬者,只是消费海量信息,把这些从你自己的认知负担中拿走,给你宁静,然后带着重要的东西来找你。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the V1 implementation of that, which many people do, is Grok Bot sits on top of Slack and it sits on top of email, and I tell it high level, "Here's my role at the company, here's kind of what I care about.
zh: 我觉得那方面的 V1 实现，很多人都在做，就是 Grok Bot 挂在 Slack 上面，也挂在邮件上面，我用高层次的指令告诉它：“这是我在公司的角色，这是我在意的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want you to notify me in these cases.
zh: 我要你在这些情况下通知我。

speaker: Unknown
en: In these cases, you don't need to ping me directly, but you should include this in your daily roundup that I read every day."
zh: 在这些情况下，你不需要直接 ping 我，但你应该把这些放进我每天读的每日汇总里。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the V1 implementation.
zh: 我觉得这就是 V1 的实现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not sure what the V10 implementation is, but maybe I'm at V3 or four, which is you can give these bots a complete fire hose of information.
zh: 我不确定 V10 的实现是什么样的，但也许我现在在 V3 或 V4，就是你可以给这些机器人一个完整的信息消防水管。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I have mine hooked up to every mention of Grok Bot ever on X, and it's interacting with our internal context.
zh: 你有什么想分享的，关于现在把这个东西推出去的 go-to-market 策略吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interacting with the QA tester to see if it can repro any bugs or feedback that we're getting.
zh: 它在和 QA 测试器交互，看能不能复现我们收到的任何 bug 或反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm hooked up to my own messaging services to quickly act on feedback and reach out to people.
zh: 我把它接到了我自己的消息服务上，以便快速对反馈采取行动并联系这些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's this just always on chief of staff entity that can preserve your focus on the things that actually matter, but is always kind of surveilling to see if there's anything that should get your attention.
zh: 我觉得就有这么一个永远在线的参谋长实体，它能让你保持专注于真正重要的事情，但同时在持续监视，看有没有什么应该引起你注意的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've seen some funny cases of people actually giving their Grok Bots, which I have not done this yet, but maybe soon, giving their Grok Bots access, the ability to page them.
zh: 我们已经看到一些有趣的案例，人们真的给了他们的 Grok Bot——我自己还没这么做，但也许快了——给他们的 Grok Bot 授权，让他们能被 call 机呼叫。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so if something super urgent happens and they're at a coffee or whatever, they get paged by Grok Bot, which is the type of thing that you only want to do if it's urgent and you really want to trust that Grok Bot does not have false positives.
zh: 所以如果发生了超级紧急的事情而他们在喝咖啡之类的，他们就会被 Grok Bot 呼叫，这种事你只有在紧急的情况下才想做，而且你必须非常信任 Grok Bot 不会产生误报。

speaker: Unknown
en: So far, those people have reported that it's been very helpful and successful.
zh: 到目前为止，那些人反馈说它非常有帮助、很成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think we're going to see more of that type of stuff where the agent or the bot should actually be more proactive to you than you reaching out to it.
zh: 但我想我们会看到更多这类东西，也就是智能体或机器人应该对你更加主动，而不是你主动去找它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that will be the next shift in AI.
zh: 我认为这将是 AI 的下一个转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a number of things that I've been very impressed with watching your team operate.
zh: 有好几件事让我在观察你们团队运作时印象非常深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is speed, which I want to talk about, but the other is how you are.
zh: 一个是速度，这个我想聊聊，另一个是你们如何。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's awareness that this is a moment in time to capture a lot of market share and really take as much of the market as you can before somebody comes around and they're like, okay, now we got something awesome, especially one of the foundation labs.
zh: 有一种意识，即这是一个需要抓住的时机，要夺取大量市场份额，在有人带着“好吧，现在我们有了很棒的东西”出现之前，尽可能多地拿下市场，尤其是某个基础模型实验室。

speaker: Unknown
en: So watching just how many free accounts you guys are giving out.
zh: 所以光是看你们发放的免费账号数量。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, the focus on use case is so smart because it's such a novel thing and you open it up and it's like, what do I do with this?
zh: 还有，对用例的关注非常聪明，因为这是个非常新颖的东西，你打开它然后就会想：我该用它做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's such a focus on, okay, here's a bunch of things people do with it.
zh: 而这里有如此强的聚焦：好，这里是一堆人们用它做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's all this talk on Twitter and just all the ways people are using a template.
zh: 然后 Twitter 上有这么多讨论，全都是人们使用模板的各种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It makes so much sense.
zh: 这非常说得通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just these two kind of focuses, from what I can tell, get as many people on as possible, as fast as possible until somebody's like, okay, because someone's going to come around and be like, all right, here's the next thing.
zh: 就这两个聚焦点，据我所见，让尽可能多的人、尽可能快地上手，直到有人说好，因为总会有人站出来说，好了，这是下一个东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Super smart and also the use case focus.
zh: 非常聪明，还有对用例的聚焦。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you were a go-to-market person at Cursor before this.
zh: 我知道你之前在 Cursor 做的是 go-to-market。

speaker: Unknown
en: Anything you want to share there about just the approach to go-to-market right now for getting this out there?
zh: 关于现在把这个产品推广出去的市场推广策略，有什么想分享的吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the pattern we saw for coding will be somewhat similar to what we see for general knowledge work.
zh: 我觉得我们在编程领域看到的模式，会与我们看到的通用知识工作模式有些相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we've learned a lot from that on the go-to-market side and more generally just building practical AI that people use.
zh: 我觉得我们在 go-to-market 方面，以及更广义地构建人们真正使用的实用 AI 方面，从中学到了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we as a company have culturally really cared about not building demoware, building actually useful stuff in the world and kind of obsessing over that.
zh: 而且我觉得我们公司在文化上非常在意不做演示软件，而是打造世界上真正有用的东西，并为之着迷。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are so many shiny objects and fun prototypes to build, but ultimately that's a very different problem than getting this in the hands of millions of people and having it transform companies.
zh: 有太多闪亮的玩具和好玩的原型可以做，但归根结底，那和把它交到数百万人手中并让它改变公司，是非常不同的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's really, I think, culturally where we've always been focused.
zh: 所以我认为，这就是我们在文化上一直聚焦的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think on the go-to-market side, what we saw for coding was a very simple pattern, which was there was an early adopter crowd.
zh: 因此在 go-to-market 方面，我们在编程领域看到的是一个非常简单的模式：有一批早期采用者。

speaker: Unknown
en: The early adopter crowd would use these coding tools and really push them to the limits, and they would mostly push them to the limits on individual projects.
zh: 这批早期采用者会使用这些编程工具并把它们推到极限，而他们主要是在个人项目上把它们推到极限。

speaker: Unknown
en: On nights and weekends, I'm thinking 2023 earlier, people would go home from work.
zh: 在晚上和周末，想想 2023 年及更早，人们下班回家。

speaker: Unknown
en: At work, they were using a basic IDE, this is pre-AI, and then at home they'd work on a side project and they'd be using Cursor or they'd be using the latest and greatest AI coding tool.
zh: 在工作时，他们用的是基础 IDE，那是 AI 之前，然后在家他们做副业项目时用 Cursor，或者用最新最强的 AI 编程工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that would give them an extreme amount of acceleration.
zh: 那会给他们带来极大量的加速。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would feel like they were experiencing the future, and then they would come back to work and they would demand it.
zh: 感觉就像在体验未来，然后他们回到工作时就会要求用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they would say, "I cannot picture working any other way than this.
zh: 他们会说：“我无法想象再用任何其他方式工作了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I feel like I'm completely walking through molasses right now.
zh: 我感觉自己现在完全是在糖浆里艰难跋涉。

speaker: Unknown
en: This needs to change."
zh: 这必须改变。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think for knowledge work, we're going to see a similar pattern of people really feeling the aha moment, sometimes in a personal capacity.
zh: 而我认为对于知识工作，我们会看到类似的模式：人们真正感受到顿悟时刻，有时是以个人身份。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we're certainly seeing a lot of this on X right now.
zh: 我觉得我们现在肯定在 X 上看到了很多这样的例子。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们认为它会改变企业，我们认为它会改变团队，机器人会进入团队并做出真正有经济价值的工作，尤其是当它们变得更聪明的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so on the go-to-market side, we're certainly making a big push on prioritizing businesses and thinking about not just the single player use case of working with a single bot, but how does a bot work inside of a broader team?

speaker: Unknown
en: How does a bot work inside of real company systems that are complicated and there's a lot of context and a lot of history to understand?
zh: 机器人如何在复杂的、有大量上下文和大量历史需要理解的真实公司系统里工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does memory look like in a broader organization versus a single individual you're catering to?
zh: 在更大的组织里，记忆是什么样的，而不是只服务单个个人？

speaker: Unknown
en: And along those lines, it's very clear you all understand the power of distribution and how you need to find both an amazing product and get distribution right because Grok Bot's amazing, but the combination of how smart you guys have been with getting it out there in all these different ways is really impressive.
zh: 沿着这个思路，很显然你们都理解分发的力量，理解你们既需要找到出色的产品、又要把分发做好，因为 Grok Bot 很出色，但你们在用这么多不同方式把它推出去上的聪明组合，真的令人印象深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that shows you what it takes these days to build something that's really successful.
zh: 我认为这向你展示了如今要打造真正成功的东西需要付出什么。

zh: 我想问问围绕这个产品和公司的不同品牌，好让人们能试着理解，因为我知道你们正在经历一场过渡、收购、SpaceX，还有这些事情。

en: So there's Grok Bot, there's Cursors.

en: So talk about the products and the way to think about these different brands today, and I know it'll probably continue to evolve just so we could communicate about it correctly.
zh: 那么谈谈这些产品，以及今天该如何看待这些不同的品牌，我知道它可能会继续演变，只是为了我们能正确地沟通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Definitely.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

en: I think there are three big pillars right now of SpaceXAI.
zh: 我认为 SpaceXAI 现在有三大支柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the first pillar is the coding product instead of products, and right now that's Cursor and Grok Build.
zh: 第一个支柱是编程产品，或者说是产品们，现在那就是 Cursor 和 Grok Build。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we're big believers that having a professional work surface for developers and for the engineering part of the organization is going to be really critical.
zh: 而且我认为我们非常相信，为开发者以及组织的工程部分打造一个专业的工作界面将是至关重要的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And right now people use Grok Bot sometimes to kick off cloud agents or to merge PRs or to do QA, a bunch of engineering adjacent tasks.
zh: 现在人们有时会用 Grok Bot 来启动 cloud 智能体，或者合并 PR，或者做 QA，一堆与工程相关的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: But ultimately when you're shipping production software, we're big believers that is going to require a product where every pixel is optimized for that end user.
zh: 但归根结底，当你要交付生产软件时，我们坚信这将需要一个为最终用户优化每一个像素的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're making big investments there.
zh: 所以我们在那里投入很大。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second category is general knowledge work, and we think bot is a really exciting step in that direction.
zh: 第二个类别是通用知识工作，我们认为 bot 是朝那个方向迈出的令人兴奋的一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's a lot more work to do of making it more useful, extending it to new surfaces, it really feeling like an AI teammate that you can delegate work to, especially inside of companies and businesses.
zh: 我认为还有很多工作要做，让它更有用，把它扩展到新的界面，让它真正感觉像一个你可以委派工作给它的 AI 队友，尤其是在公司和企业内部。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's kind of the second pillar.
zh: 所以这是第二个支柱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then third is the general model effort.
zh: 然后第三个是通用模型方面的努力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to train the smartest models in the world that are really capable.
zh: 我们想要训练世界上最聪明、真正有能力的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one thing that somewhat distinguishes SpaceXAI from other AI labs is I think our goal is less to build, chase super intelligence or some kind of vague aspirational ideal.
zh: 而且我认为 SpaceXAI 与其他 AI 实验室有所区别的一点是，我认为我们的目标与其说是构建、追逐超级智能或某种模糊的理想化愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the goal is actually very practical, which is to build useful AI.
zh: 而目标实际上非常务实，那就是构建有用的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we do that on the product side, we do that on the model side.
zh: 我们在产品侧这样做，我们也在模型侧这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think part of that is also just cultural of the group of people contributing to these models are engineers and people who came into the model training effort from a very applied mindset.
zh: 而且我认为其中一部分也是文化上的，为这些模型做贡献的人们是工程师，是从非常应用的思维方式进入模型训练工作的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's what gets this company going and I think is actually a slightly different direction from some of the other competitors out there.
zh: 而且我认为这就是推动这家公司前进的东西，我认为这实际上与其他一些竞争对手的方向略有不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: Super interesting.
zh: 非常有意思。

en: Okay, there's a couple directions I want to go.
zh: 好，有几个方向我想去探讨。

en: One is you have this tweet that is, I think you pinned it or maybe it's your last tweet.
zh: 一个是你有一条推文，我想是你置顶了，或者是你最近的一条推文。

en: It's up there in your timeline if people check you out.
zh: 它就在你的时间线上，如果人们去看看你的话。

en: So the tweet is, "An AI that does 100% of the job feels categorically different from one that gets you 90% there.
zh: 那条推文是：“一个能完成 100% 工作的 AI，与一个能帮你完成 90% 的 AI，感觉上是截然不同的。

en: I've significantly updated what I think AI is capable of."
zh: 我已经大幅更新了我对 AI 能力的看法。”

zh: 多说一些关于这个的。

en: I think for me, what made me so excited to work on Grok Bot and contribute to it is it was the first time for non-coding tasks that I felt like I could truly delegate work to AI and not have to think about it and I would come back and it's done.
zh: 我认为对我来说，让我如此兴奋地参与开发 Grok Bot 并为之做贡献的是，这是第一次在非编程任务上，我感觉我可以真正把工作委派给 AI 而不用去操心它，然后我回来时它已经完成了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think engineers have been feeling this for quite some time, for maybe a year, a year and a half, things have been like that.
zh: 而且我认为工程师们已经有这种感觉相当长一段时间了，大概一年、一年半，事情一直是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the job of a developer has completely transformed.
zh: 我是说，开发者的工作已经彻底转变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is unrecognizable from what it was two years ago and many, many words have been said on that topic.
zh: 与两年前相比已经完全认不出来了，关于这个话题已经说了很多很多话。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think it's underrated how different that experience is from what most people are feeling about AI right now and the way that AI has changed their lives.
zh: 但我认为人们低估了那种体验与现在大多数人对 AI 的感受、以及 AI 改变他们生活的方式有多么不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it looks quite similar to the way that people would use AI two years ago where you create a new thread for a task, you type it into an input box, you hit enter, you watch all of these steps happen, you get an output, it's not quite right, you keep working on it.
zh: 它看起来与人们两年前使用 AI 的方式非常相似：你为一个任务创建一个新对话，把它输入到一个输入框，按下回车，你看着所有这些步骤发生，你得到一个输出，它不太对，你继续在它上面工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And Grok Bot, I think short circuits a lot of that.
zh: 而 Grok Bot，我认为短路了很多这样的过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you first lay eyes on the first screen, you're like, "Whoa, this is clearly different.
zh: 当你第一次看到第一个屏幕时，你会想：“哇，这显然不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's see if it actually works, but this is different."
zh: 让我们看看它是否真的有效，但这不一样。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you give it something and it kind of works to a surprising extent.
zh: 然后你给它一些东西，它在相当惊人的程度上有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we're going to do a lot to make it work much better.
zh: 而且我认为我们会做很多工作让它好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think what I was expressing in that was when you have a teammate that you only 90% trust and you give something to, which luckily I do not have the experience of here because I work with great people, but if you delegate something to someone and you're like, "I know I'm going to have to be thinking about this while you're doing it, and I know it probably is not going to be quite there and I'm going to have to intervene and steer it slightly," that's not 90% task completion.
zh: 所以我想我在那条推文里表达的是，当你有一个只有 90% 信任度的队友，你把东西交给它——幸运的是我在这里没有这种经历，因为我与很棒的人共事——但如果你把某件事委派给某人，然后你想：“我知道在你做这件事的时候我将不得不一直惦记着它，而且我知道它可能不会完全到位，我将不得不介入并稍微引导一下，”那就不是 90% 的任务完成度。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're still doing the thing and it feels that way and it's weighing on you in the same way versus truly throwing a no look pass to a colleague and being like, "You got this, here's the context, go off and run.
zh: 你仍然在做那件事，感觉也是那样，它同样压在你身上，而不是真正地给同事来一记不看人的传球，然后说：“你可以搞定，这是背景信息，放手去干吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited to see what you do."
zh: 我很期待看到你做出的成果。”

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a different category.
zh: 那是另一个类别。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the type of thing that people feel with Grok Bot every day are these no look passes and you just trust that it can get it done and then it does and it's just a very magical experience.
zh: 而且我认为这就是人们每天用 Grok Bot 时感受到的东西，就是这些不看人的传球，你就是相信它能搞定，然后它就搞定了，这是一种非常神奇的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I've had that experience consistently.
zh: 是的，我一直都有这种体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay, so another element of how y'all operate that has really impressed me and I've not seen this before is how fast y'all move.
zh: 好，那么你们运作方式的另一个让我印象深刻、而我以前从未见过的方面是你们行动有多快。

en: So I got added to this Slack as I was giving feedback with some folks and it's just like, okay, how about, okay, tomorrow we're going to give you some free codes to give out.
zh: 所以我在和一些 folks 反馈的时候被拉进了一个 Slack，然后就变成这样：好，怎么样，好，明天我们给你一些免费码让你分发。

en: We'll do this tomorrow.

zh: 或者说我们要上线一个带模板的市场,我们两天内就要上线这个。

en: It's just like, what?
zh: 就像,什么?

en: I don't have time for this.
zh: 我没时间搞这个。
