speaker: Unknown
en: So there's kind of two parts of this question, just what's the secret to how fast you all have been moving and how do you stay aligned moving that fast towards a vision that you all believe in and where you want it to go versus just band-aiding it along the way?
zh: 所以这个问题有两部分,一是你们移动得这么快的秘诀是什么,二是你们在移动这么快的情况下如何保持对齐,朝着你们都相信的愿景和你们想要的方向前进,而不是一路上只是打补丁?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing I've been really happy has never changed is that startup feeling inside of the company.
zh: 有一件事我一直很高兴从未改变,那就是公司内部的创业感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for context, when I joined Cursor originally, we were about 15 people.
zh: 作为背景,当我最初加入 Cursor 时,我们大约 15 个人。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 我们扩张到了超过一千人。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 注:SpXAI。 [[560]] 当你和这群极其有才华的人在一起时,成为其中一员是非常有趣的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's something that is just so fun to be a part of when you're around this group of incredibly talented people.
zh: 当你身边都是这群才华横溢的人时，参与其中真的是一件非常有趣的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's moving a hundred miles an hour.
zh: 每个人都在以一百英里的时速前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: You trust, you deeply trust everybody to execute on their part of the equation.
zh: 你信任,你深深地信任每个人去执行他们在整个等式中负责的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a clear vision that everyone is fired up about and knows that they need to execute on.
zh: 而且有一个清晰的愿景,每个人都为之振奋,并知道自己需要去执行。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as companies grow, and we've had the fortune of hiring really great people from other companies that have gone through hyper growth, things slow down and you kind of keep telling yourself, we're still a startup, we still move quickly, but you really don't and everyone knows that you don't and it's easier to say than to actually be.
zh: 随着公司成长,而我们有幸从其他经历过高速增长的公司招聘了非常优秀的人,事情会变慢,你会不断告诉自己,我们仍然是一家初创公司,我们仍然行动迅速,但你其实并不是,而且每个人都知道你不是,说出来比真正做到要容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: And fingers crossed, this continues to be true.

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's really critical for our success if this continues to be true.
zh: 我认为如果这一点继续保持,这对我们的成功非常关键。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even as we scaled, it has always felt like that startup that I first joined.
zh: 但即使我们扩张了,它一直感觉像我最初加入的那家初创公司。

en: And I think if you define a startup by number of people or by the funding round, none of those things really make any sense.

speaker: Unknown
en: The core thing that defines a startup is exactly what you're describing, which is this kind of scramble energy of things are kind of chaotic and kind of disorganized.
zh: 定义初创公司的核心恰恰是你所描述的,就是那种慌乱冲劲,事情有点混乱、有点无组织。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for a lot of people, that's not a pleasant working environment to be in, but it has these amazing properties of you can make extreme impact in a particular direction in a short amount of time and you really do get out of the system what you put in.
zh: 对很多人来说,这不是一个令人愉快的工作环境,但它有这些奇妙的特性:你可以在短时间内朝特定方向产生极端影响,而且你从这个系统中得到的确实与你投入的成正比。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think as a culture, I think as an organization and the way we construct ourselves, it's really been to enable that property in a way that I think some of our competitors and other AI labs have gotten much bigger and you can feel it.
zh: 所以我认为作为一种文化,我认为作为一个组织以及我们构建自己的方式,一直都是为了实现这种特性,而我认为我们的一些竞争对手和其他 AI 实验室已经变得庞大得多,你能感觉到。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think us, even as we scale, there is that start-upy impulse that is quite important to move quickly on these things.
zh: 而我认为我们,即使我们扩张,仍然有那种初创公司式的冲劲,这对于在这些事情上快速行动非常重要。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 让我顺着这条线问下去,问你这个我一直期待问你的大问题。

zh: 如果你从外部看 Cursor,它本不该成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: It shouldn't have lasted because, one, it's in the most competitive market in the world competing against the fastest growing companies in history, OpenAI and Anthropic.
zh: 它本不该存续,因为,第一,它身处世界上最竞争激烈的市场,与历史上增长最快的公司 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 竞争。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's one.
zh: 这是第一。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like the competition is unlike anything anyone's ever experienced.
zh: 这种竞争激烈程度是任何人从未经历过的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, it sits on top of those platforms to power it.
zh: 第二,它建立在那些平台之上以获得支撑。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I've seen as an outsider is what has allowed Cursor to win and have this massive exit and continue to succeed is how quickly you all adjust to the reality of the market.
zh: 而我作为外部人所看到的,让 Cursor 能够获胜、实现这次巨大退出并持续成功的,是你们适应市场现实的速度有多快。

speaker: Unknown
en: Started as auto complete and then things moved on to just talking to agents and then into the cloud and now Grok Bot.
zh: 从自动补全开始,然后事情发展到与智能体对话,然后进入云端,现在是 Grok Bot。

speaker: Unknown
en: To me, that feels like a core part of the success is quickly adjusting to reality and also building the best in class experience for a thing that also exists other places.
zh: 对我来说,成功的一个核心部分就是快速适应现实,同时也为一个在其他地方也存在的东西构建同类最佳的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Grok Bot's a great example.
zh: Grok Bot 就是一个很好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could do this other places, but it's the best in class experience, Cursor, the ID, the best way to code.
zh: 你可以在其他地方做到这一点,但这是同类最佳的体验,Cursor 这个 ID,最好的编程方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's my question.
zh: 所以这就是我的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I answered it, but what do you think has been core to Cursor's ability to not just survive in this crazy competitive market, but do so incredibly well consistently for so long?
zh: 也许我已经回答了它,但你认为什么是 Cursor 不仅能在这么疯狂竞争的市场中生存下来,而且能如此长时间持续表现出色的核心?

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, a lot of this, and it's a fuzzy answer, a lot of this I think is downstream from culture and the culture that you set and the people that you bring in and the way that they approach these problems.
zh: 我的意思是,很多这个,这是个模糊的答案,我认为很多这是文化的下游结果,是你设定的文化、你引入的人,以及他们处理这些问题的方式。

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而我认为对我们来说,正如你所说,我们从未自满。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've never felt like we've won, and it's always been about the next thing.
zh: 我们从未觉得自己已经赢了,一直都是关于下一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's been a really deep belief across the company that AI is moving incredibly quickly.
zh: 而且我认为整个公司有一种非常深入的信念,即 AI 正在以令人难以置信的速度发展。
